mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with a 3-month FEDFUNDS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4.5% indicates a tight labor market that increases corporate profit margins and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts and retail sales indicate robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and generates positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a decline in industrial production signals an economic slowdown that depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when INDPRO declines and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% indicates a strengthening economy, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters with GDPC1 > 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment and decreases in unemployment indicate a robust labor market that drives consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a rise in the federal funds rate signals aggressive monetary tightening that depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% in more than 55% of cases.
